title: Das bunte Leben
estimate_note: Christie's published no range ("estimate on request"). Range as reported by The Art Newspaper (high £25m) and Whitebank (£18m to £25m). Apollo gives £18m to £35m, which would put the £27m hammer inside the estimate.
seller: Heirs of Hedwig Lewenstein-Weyermann, following restitution in 2023
bidding_notes: Won by a phone bidder represented by Maria Los of Christie's client advisory, Americas, after about six minutes, per The Art Newspaper and Artnet.
why_it_matters: The top lot of the London season was a restituted picture with a third-party guarantee behind it. Clean title plus a pre-arranged floor is how the biggest consignments now get to market.

image.credit: Photograph by Ermell, via Wikimedia Commons

update_note: 14 Nov 2026: lot number added from Christie's lot page; estimate note now says the house published no range.

title: Composition III (Komposition No. XIII)
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by The Art Newspaper.
bidding_notes: Won by a phone bidder represented by Katharine Arnold of Christie's, per The Art Newspaper.
why_it_matters: First time at auction, hammered near the low estimate, and guaranteed by a third party. The headline price is strong; the bidding was thin.

sale_name: Monsoon: The Peter Simon Collection Evening Sale
title: Figure in Movement
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Apollo.
seller: Collection of Peter Simon, founder of Monsoon
bidding_notes: Sold to a bidder in the room (Christie's). The auctioneer described the buyer as a woman in the room, per The Art Newspaper.
financing_notes: All 41 lots in the Simon sale were guaranteed, 11 by Christie's and the rest by third parties, per The Art Newspaper. The backer of this lot is not stated.
why_it_matters: The lead lot of Christie's highest-value single-owner sale in London went to someone sitting in the room, which is rare at this price.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed. The Art Newspaper reports that all 41 lots in this sale were guaranteed; the backer of this lot is not stated.

sale_name: Monsoon: The Peter Simon Collection Evening Sale
title: Composition A, with Double Line and Yellow
financing_notes: All 41 lots in the Simon sale were guaranteed, 11 by Christie's and the rest by third parties, per The Art Newspaper. The backer of this lot is not stated.
why_it_matters: This painting failed to sell at Christie's London in 2014. Twelve years and a famous collection name later, it sold.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed. The Art Newspaper reports that all 41 lots in this sale were guaranteed; the backer of this lot is not stated.

sale_name: Monsoon: The Peter Simon Collection Evening Sale

financing_notes: All 41 lots in the Simon sale were guaranteed, 11 by Christie's and the rest by third parties, per The Art Newspaper. The backer of this lot is not stated.
why_it_matters: An auction debut from the artist's 1925 'dream' paintings. Fresh-to-market works carried this sale.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed. The Art Newspaper reports that all 41 lots in this sale were guaranteed; the backer of this lot is not stated.

sale_name: Monsoon: The Peter Simon Collection Evening Sale
title: Painterly Architectonic
estimate_note: Low estimate £1.8m (Christie's). High estimate not stated.
buyer_attribution: art advisers in London and New York; reported by Apollo, citing the Baer Faxt newsletter. Whether the firm bought for a client is not stated
bidding_notes: Eight minutes of bidding in the room and on phones (Christie's). Artnet reports the winning bid was taken by Christie's president Alex Rotter.
financing_notes: All 41 lots in the Simon sale were guaranteed, 11 by Christie's and the rest by third parties, per The Art Newspaper. The backer of this lot is not stated.
record: Auction record for the artist, per Artnet.
why_it_matters: Hammered at more than three times the low estimate after eight minutes of bidding, and reported sold to an advisory firm. Advisers bid when a client wants the work and not the attention.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed. The Art Newspaper reports that all 41 lots in this sale were guaranteed; the backer of this lot is not stated.

sale_name: Monsoon: The Peter Simon Collection Evening Sale
title: Last House
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Observer.
bidding_notes: Three phone bidders competed, per The Art Newspaper.
financing_notes: All 41 lots in the Simon sale were guaranteed, 11 by Christie's and the rest by third parties, per The Art Newspaper. The backer of this lot is not stated.
why_it_matters: A living painter at nearly three times the low estimate, with three phone bidders. Demand for the top British contemporary names is intact.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed. The Art Newspaper reports that all 41 lots in this sale were guaranteed; the backer of this lot is not stated.

sale_name: Monsoon: The Peter Simon Collection Evening Sale
title: Streak 2
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Observer. Compared against the price with fees because the hammer price was not reported.
financing_notes: All 41 lots in the Simon sale were guaranteed, 11 by Christie's and the rest by third parties, per The Art Newspaper. The backer of this lot is not stated.
why_it_matters: A solid price inside the estimate for a blue-chip British name. Useful as a baseline, not a breakout.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed. The Art Newspaper reports that all 41 lots in this sale were guaranteed; the backer of this lot is not stated.

title: Untitled
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Art Centron.
bidding_notes: Bidding opened at £7m, per The Art Newspaper.
financing_notes: Reported as guaranteed by The Art Newspaper. Type of guarantee not stated.
record: Highest auction price for de Kooning in Europe, per The Art Newspaper.
why_it_matters: A European record for the artist that hammered barely above its low estimate, with a guarantee in place. Records and weak bidding now turn up in the same lot.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed, matching the press report already quoted in the financing note. The type of guarantee is not stated.

title: Abstraktes Bild
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Art Centron.
why_it_matters: Hammered below the low estimate; fees carried it over the line. It last sold for £3.6m in 2011, so the price still nearly doubled.

title: Untitled
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Art Centron.
seller: Consignor bought it at auction in 1992, per Art Centron
bidding_notes: Sold to an online bidder, per The Art Newspaper.
financing_notes: Reported as guaranteed by The Art Newspaper. Type not stated.
why_it_matters: A guaranteed work on paper that sold at its low estimate to an online bidder. Seven-figure art is now bought on a screen without comment.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed, matching the press report already quoted in the financing note. The type of guarantee is not stated.

title: Mathis
estimate_note: Low estimate £6m, per Whitebank. High estimate not stated.
bidding_notes: Won by a phone bidder represented by Phillips chairman Robert Manley, per Observer.
why_it_matters: Phillips' top London lot came in under its low estimate even with fees, in a sale where every lot sold. A full sell-through can hide soft prices.

sale_name: La Collection Schlumberger: Le Temps retrouvé
title: Iris
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Reuters and The Art Newspaper. Compared against the price with fees because the hammer price was not reported.
bidding_notes: Six bidders over about 45 minutes. Won by a private collector in Asia bidding by phone through Jen Hua of Sotheby's Asia, per Reuters, The Art Newspaper and Artnet.
financing_notes: No lot in the sale was guaranteed, per MutualArt.
record: Highest price for any artwork at auction in France, per Reuters.
why_it_matters: The most expensive artwork ever sold at auction in France, with no guarantee and six bidders over 45 minutes. It went to Asia by phone, in Paris rather than New York.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: lot number and date of the work added from Sotheby's lot page. The lot page shows the estimate but no sold price, so the price stays press-reported.

sale_name: La Collection Schlumberger: Le Temps retrouvé
title: Saule pleureur (L'Arbre de feu)
estimate_note: Artnet reports €9.6m; Observer and MutualArt report €9.7m.
financing_notes: No lot in the sale was guaranteed, per MutualArt.
why_it_matters: A late Giverny picture from the same collection. Single-owner sales with one star lot lift everything around it.

title: Espace non-descriptif
record: Record for the artist in France and his second-highest price at auction, per MutualArt.
why_it_matters: A French record for an artist outside the usual top ten names. Paris is where early abstraction is being repriced.

title: Tête crâne
estimate_note: More than four times the low estimate, per Observer. Figures not stated.
why_it_matters: A 1934 plaster, first of its kind at auction, at more than four times its low estimate. Rarity beat medium.

title: Bord des falaises à Pourville
estimate_note: Compared against the price with fees because the hammer price was not reported.
why_it_matters: Sold by the descendants of the dealer who made Impressionism a market. Provenance like that is the product.

title: Jeunes filles au bord de la mer
estimate_note: Compared against the price with fees because the hammer price was not reported.
why_it_matters: Within estimate in a sale where all 27 lots sold. Orderly, which is what a family seller wants.

title: Un Verger
estimate_note: Compared against the price with fees because the hammer price was not reported.
why_it_matters: More than double the high estimate with fees for a picture the family had held since acquiring it, with a third-party guarantee in place.

sale_name: 20th/21st Century: Paris Evening Sale including Thinking Italian
title: Concetto spaziale, Mezzogiorno in Piazza S. Marco
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Observer. Compared against the price with fees because the hammer price was not reported. Sale date taken from MutualArt; Christie's release does not state it.
why_it_matters: First time at auction and the top Italian lot of the Paris week. Postwar Italian art sells better in Paris than anywhere else right now.

sale_name: 20th/21st Century: Paris Evening Sale including Thinking Italian
title: Minoutcha
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Observer. Compared against the price with fees. Sale date taken from MutualArt.
financing_notes: Reported as guaranteed by Observer. Type not stated.
why_it_matters: Off the market for 25 years, guaranteed, and sold in the middle of its estimate. A pre-arranged result.
update_note: 14 Nov 2026: guarantee changed from unknown to guaranteed, matching the press report already quoted in the financing note. The type of guarantee is not stated.

sale_name: Une demeure princière: The residence of Sheikh Hamad bin Abdullah Al Thani, Part III
title: Desk
estimate_note: Sale series ran 4 to 9 November; the exact session date is not confirmed. Compared against the price with fees.
seller: Sheikh Hamad bin Abdullah Al Thani
why_it_matters: Art Deco from a named royal residence at double the high estimate. In design, who owned it moves the price more than who made it.

title: Chronomètre à Résonance 'Régence', platinum
estimate_note: Estimate: in excess of CHF 1,000,000. Prices include buyer's premium, confirmed by the reported hammer price on the top lot. Sale ran 7 to 8 November; session date per lot not confirmed.
bidding_notes: Won by a phone bidder represented by Phillips specialist Alex Ghotbi. The underbidder in the room was Shawn Mehta of F.P. Journe's London boutique, per Hodinkee.
record: World record for the reference, per Phillips.
why_it_matters: A watch by a living maker at CHF 8.7m against an estimate of 'in excess of CHF 1m', in what Phillips calls the first live watch auction to pass $100m. Independent watchmaking is now priced like blue-chip art.

title: Ref. 1436 split-seconds chronograph, stainless steel
estimate_note: Prices include buyer's premium, confirmed by the reported hammer price on the top lot. Sale ran 7 to 8 November; session date per lot not confirmed.
record: Auction record for any split-seconds chronograph, per Phillips.
why_it_matters: The same watch made $3.29m in 2015, per Hodinkee. It more than doubled in eleven years.

title: Chronomètre à Résonance 'Tokyo Boutique', titanium
estimate_note: Prices include buyer's premium, confirmed by the reported hammer price on the top lot. Sale ran 7 to 8 November; session date per lot not confirmed.
why_it_matters: Nearly eight times the high estimate with fees. When estimates are this far off, they are marketing, not valuation.

title: Vagabondage III, diamond-set platinum
estimate_note: Prices include buyer's premium, confirmed by the reported hammer price on the top lot. Sale ran 7 to 8 November; session date per lot not confirmed.
why_it_matters: One of four Journe watches in the top five lots of the sale. One maker is carrying the top of this market.

title: Chronomètre à Résonance 'Pre-Production' No. 022/99R, platinum
estimate_note: Prices include buyer's premium, confirmed by the reported hammer price on the top lot. Sale ran 7 to 8 November; session date per lot not confirmed.
buyer_attribution: head of F.P. Journe's London boutique; reported by Hodinkee, which says he later told its author he bid for a friend and not for the brand
bidding_notes: Phillips withdrew its claim that this was the first pre-production Résonance sold or delivered, per Hodinkee.
why_it_matters: The winning paddle belonged to the head of the maker's own London boutique, who says he bid for a friend. Insiders bidding at auction shapes prices and deserves scrutiny.

title: Portico Mystery Clock No. 4
estimate_note: Prices include buyer's premium, confirmed by the reported hammer price on the top lot. Sale ran 7 to 8 November; session date per lot not confirmed.
why_it_matters: A clock, not a wristwatch, in the top six. Buyers at this level are paying for objects, not wearability.

sale_name: Rare Watches Including Watches for ELA
title: Vagabondage, pink gold (top lot of a matching trilogy)
estimate_note: Each of the three reported with an estimate of CHF 400,000 to 800,000 (Time on the Move). Christie's does not say whether its lot prices include premium; treated as including premium. Hodinkee gives a lower combined figure of CHF 4,756,200.
bidding_notes: All three watches went to the same private collector (Christie's), bidding through a Christie's specialist (Hodinkee). Combined CHF 6,709,200.
why_it_matters: One collector bought all three matching-number watches for CHF 6.7m combined. Buying the set is how a serious collector takes a category off the table.

title: Ref. 3970 perpetual calendar chronograph, yellow gold, first numbered example
estimate_note: Sale ran 8 to 9 November; session not confirmed. Robb Report gives $2.3m.
record: Record for the reference, per Robb Report.
why_it_matters: A record for a reference long seen as the affordable Patek complication. 'First of' is the provenance watch buyers pay for.

sale_name: Magnificent Jewels Including the Bulgari Pink
title: The Bulgari Pink, 24.00-carat fancy intense pink diamond ring
estimate_note: Estimate as reported by Rapaport. Compared against the price with fees because the hammer price was not reported.
seller: A European noble family; acquired in India by the consignor's great-grandparents in the 1950s
bidding_notes: Buyer not named. Christie's head of jewellery Max Fawcett told the dpa news agency the buyer bought the ring to give as a gift and to see it worn, per La Sicilia.
why_it_matters: Seventy years in one European family, then sold inside its estimate. A portable, private store of value coming back to market on the family's terms.
update_note: 15 Nov 2026: bidding note added. Christie's says the buyer intends the ring as a gift; still unnamed.

title: 499P Modificata
estimate_note: Estimate: in excess of CHF 7,500,000.
record: First Ferrari 499P sold at public auction (Christie's).
why_it_matters: A barely driven, track-only car the buyer cannot take home: it stays at Ferrari in Maranello until December 2028 and runs through a factory programme. This is a car bought as an asset.

title: F50
bidding_notes: Sold to a bidder in the room, per Broad Arrow.
record: Auction record for the model, per Broad Arrow.
why_it_matters: A 106-mile car setting the model record. The premium is for not using it.

sources.publisher: Broad Arrow Auctions release, via FinancialContent

title: Daytona SP3
estimate_note: Sold above its high estimate, per Broad Arrow. Figures not stated.
record: Auction record for a non-charity example, per Broad Arrow.
why_it_matters: A one-year-old car resold by its first owner above the high estimate. Allocation from the factory is the real asset.

sources.publisher: Broad Arrow Auctions release, via FinancialContent

record: Auction record for a Cartier bracelet, per Lumière Gems citing Sotheby's
title: The Romanov Sapphire, 197.80-carat unheated Ceylon sapphire set in a bracelet
bidding_notes: Sold to a private collector, per AP. Worn by Empress Maria Feodorovna of Russia; sold by the Soviet state; bought in 1927 by the opera singer Ganna Walska; sold by Sotheby's in New York in 1971 and in Geneva in 1992, per NBC News and Town & Country.
why_it_matters: A stone with three earlier auction appearances made 2.4 times its high estimate. The sapphire did not change. The story attached to it did. Royal provenance is the one premium in this market that compounds every time an object resells.

title: Unmounted 8.63-carat Fancy Intense Pink diamond, type IIa, VS2
bidding_notes: Rapaport reports a private buyer. Il Sole 24 Ore gives CHF 4,488,000; Rapaport and National Jeweler round to CHF 4.5 million.
why_it_matters: The top lot of Sotheby's Geneva jewels week was a loose stone with no maker and no story. Pink diamonds are priced like a scarce commodity: carat, colour grade, type. It landed inside its range, which is what a liquid asset does.

title: Unmounted 51.79-carat unheated Tanzanian spinel
bidding_notes: Il Sole 24 Ore gives CHF 1,664,000; Rapaport and National Jeweler round to CHF 1.7 million. Moussaieff is a London family jeweller and gem dealer, which suggests it bought for stock or a client.
why_it_matters: A dealer paid more than three times the high estimate for a stone most buyers could not name. When the trade outbids private collectors, it is betting it can sell the stone again for more. Spinel is being repriced from understudy to lead.

title: Black opal and diamond tiara, convertible to a necklace and brooch, worn at the 1953 coronation
seller: From the Devonshire family, per Royal Watcher and the Financial Times
bidding_notes: Price as given by Royal Watcher and Lumière Gems; the Financial Times gives CHF 1.66 million and National Jeweler CHF 1.7 million.
why_it_matters: Opal is not a premium gem on its own. The coronation and the family name did the work, about 50% over the high estimate.

title: Unmounted 8.11-carat Fancy Pink diamond, VVS1
estimate_note: JCK and other previews give CHF 1.7 million to 2.5 million; Rapaport gives CHF 1.5 million to 2.5 million, which would put the price inside the range.
bidding_notes: No buyer reported. Il Sole 24 Ore gives CHF 1,561,600; Rapaport rounds to CHF 1.6 million.
why_it_matters: Same sale, same colour family, half a carat smaller and one grade paler than the top lot, and it sold for about a third of the price. Colour grade is the whole price in pink diamonds.

title: Ring set with a 2.88-carat Fancy Deep Blue diamond
bidding_notes: Offered without reserve, per Rapaport, so it had to sell. Il Sole 24 Ore gives CHF 1,536,000; Rapaport rounds to CHF 1.5 million.
why_it_matters: No reserve means the seller accepted whatever the room would pay. The room paid less than the low estimate even with fees. That is a clean read of demand for small blue diamonds.

title: Belle Époque brooch set with a 23.64-carat padparadscha sapphire
seller: Previously owned by Princess Sibylla of Sweden and then Princess Birgitta of Sweden, per Royal Watcher and Hola
bidding_notes: Two phone bidders, per Royal Watcher. Price as given by Royal Watcher and Moral Moda; National Jeweler gives CHF 1.1 million and Lumière Gems CHF 1.2 million. Hola reports that King Carl XVI Gustaf opposed the sale of the family jewels.
why_it_matters: An estimate of CHF 40,000 to 60,000 became CHF 1.12 million, almost 19 times the high estimate. The stone is good. The princesses are why two phones would not stop.

record: Highest price for any Star Wars collectible at auction, per Heritage and ARTnews. The previous high was $3.875 million for a Tom Jung poster; a Luke Skywalker lightsaber made $3.75 million in July 2026.
sale_name: Heritage Auctions Ultimate Star Wars Auction
title: Darth Vader hero dueling lightsaber, screen-matched to The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi
bidding_notes: No buyer named. Heritage's release and ARTnews do not say whether the price includes the buyer's premium; Heritage normally publishes results with it. Recorded as premium-inclusive; not confirmed.
why_it_matters: A film prop beat every Star Wars object ever sold, and the record has been broken twice in four months. The buyers who grew up on these films now have the money that once went into Old Master drawings.

title: Homme assis
bidding_notes: Won by a telephone bidder, per Yicai, which also gives the CNY 10 million hammer.
why_it_matters: The top lot of Christie's Shanghai evening was a late Picasso on panel, bought by a phone bidder. Mainland Chinese buyers were Christie's biggest buyer market in Asia-Pacific in the first half of 2026. They are buying Western names at home now, not only in Hong Kong.

title: Pumpkin
bidding_notes: No buyer reported.
why_it_matters: Inside the estimate with fees, so the hammer was likely near the low end. Kusama pumpkins trade like a blue chip: steady, priced to the range, no fireworks.

title: Mars - 03.04.2003
bidding_notes: No buyer reported. ARTSK reports the painting made about $2.46 million at Ravenel in Taipei in 2019, so the seller likely took a loss of roughly a quarter before costs. Not confirmed by a second source.
why_it_matters: A late Zao Wou-Ki sold inside its range and still lost money for the seller, if the 2019 price ARTSK reports is right. Zao's market has cooled since its 2018 peak. Inside the estimate is not the same as a good result.

title: Miffy the Artist after Dick Bruna
estimate_note: Above the high estimate only with fees included; Christie's did not publish the hammer.
bidding_notes: No buyer reported.
why_it_matters: A living Chinese painter cleared his high estimate in his home market. Liu Ye is one of the few mainland contemporary names with a deep enough bench of buyers to do that in a soft year.

title: 'Starlight' coloured diamond and diamond necklace, centred on a 90.80-carat pear-shaped diamond
bidding_notes: No buyer reported. Christie's lot notes say the 90.80-carat centre stone is graded W to X, Light Brown, and that the coloured diamonds have not been tested for natural colour.
why_it_matters: The biggest stone of the week sold below its low estimate even with fees. Size did not carry it. A light brown grade and an untested-colour caveat in the catalogue did the damage. Buyers paid for certainty in Geneva and refused to pay for doubt in Shanghai.
